question.prompt: How many non-congruent right triangles are there such that the perimeter in cm and area in \(\text{cm}^2\) are numerically equal?

solutions.explanation:
Scaling changes perimeter and area at different rates, which lets us make them numerically equal. Measure lengths in centimeters, and let \(P>0\) and \(K>0\) be the numerical perimeter and area of any nondegenerate right triangle.

Multiplying every side by a positive factor \(t\) multiplies the perimeter by \(t\) and the area by \(t^2\). Thus the desired equality becomes
\[
tP=t^2K.
\]
Since \(t>0\), this holds exactly when
\[
t=\frac{P}{K}.
\]
This factor is positive, so every right-triangle shape produces a triangle satisfying the condition.

Now start with right triangles having legs \(1\) and \(n\), for each positive integer \(n\). Apply the scaling just described to each one. Their longer-leg-to-shorter-leg ratios are \(n\), and scaling preserves these ratios. Distinct values of \(n\) therefore produce noncongruent triangles. Hence there are \(\boxed{\text{infinitely many}}\), choice \(\boxed{\text{E}}\).
solutions.title: Scale each right-triangle shape
